title: The One Room and the Cotai Strip: Adelson from Dorchester to the Mount of Olives
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Dorchester, Boston, the one room
stops.date_confidence: Attested day, month and year: Wikipedia, 'Sheldon Adelson', and every major obituary give 4 August 1933, Boston. The Boston Globe and Legacy.com listings returned 403 on fetch and were not read directly. The coordinate is the Dorchester neighborhood, not a street address: no source reached names the building.
stops.campa: Sheldon Gary Adelson is born in Boston on the fourth of August and raised in a single room in Dorchester, shared with his parents and three siblings. The family is Jewish, immigrant, and poor in the ordinary way of the neighborhood, where a room is a room and nobody in it expects a second one. He will tell the story of this room for the next seventy years, in boardrooms and on witness stands. His father Arthur drives a taxi and his mother Sarah keeps a knitting shop, and no source reached names the street the four children slept on.
suggested_refs: Connie Bruck, 'The Brass Ring,' The New Yorker, 30 June 2008, on the Dorchester household
sources: Connie Bruck, 'The Brass Ring,' The New Yorker, 30 June 2008

stops.name: Downtown Boston, the two hundred dollars
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The age is contested in the pool itself: Wikipedia gives ten, which from an August 1933 birth places the episode in 1943 or 1944; other retellings give twelve and about 1945. Month and day are defaults and are not sourced. The coordinate is downtown Boston near Downtown Crossing, a stand-in for corners no source names individually.
stops.campa: He borrows two hundred dollars from an uncle and buys the right to sell newspapers at street corners downtown, where the traffic is thickest and the pitches belong to whoever paid for them first. He is ten years old. The transaction is his own account of himself, retold in every profile and in the company's official history: not the labor of selling papers but the purchase of the position from which papers can be sold. Whether the uncle's two hundred dollars ever changed hands, no document reached says.
suggested_refs: The Las Vegas Sands corporate history at sands.com/company/our-story, which carries the newsstand story as founding legend
sources: Connie Bruck, 'The Brass Ring,' The New Yorker, 30 June 2008

stops.name: Dorchester filling stations, the candy machines
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction with an internal contradiction the pool did not resolve: Wikipedia gives age fifteen, a ten thousand dollar loan, and the year 1948; the dossier's geography lens gives sixteen and the late nineteen forties. Month and day are defaults. The coordinate is Dorchester, since the stations are described only as the ones his father's cab used.
stops.campa: At fifteen he borrows ten thousand dollars and puts candy vending machines into filling stations across the neighborhood, including the stations where his father's cab takes on gasoline. The machines work while he is at school. It is the second business before adulthood and it has the shape of the first: buy the placement, then let the placement earn. Boston taxi drivers feed coins into a schoolboy's boxes all through the late nineteen forties. The size of the loan comes from him and from nobody else.
suggested_refs: The vending-machine route as told in the Sands corporate biography and in obituary retellings
sources: Las Vegas Sands corporate history, sands.com/company/our-story

stops.name: City College of New York, the degree not taken
stops.date_confidence: Attested that he attended and left without a degree; the years are given only as the early nineteen fifties, so 1951 with defaulted month and day is an ordering device. The Army service, roughly 1953 and reportedly as a court reporter, is folded in here because no source reached names a post or a base. The coordinate is the Convent Avenue campus, inherited byte-identical from bob_kahn.journey.json, which is the only City College pin the corpus carries.
stops.campa: He enrolls at City College of New York, on the Convent Avenue campus in Harlem, the free municipal college of the children of immigrants, and reads real estate and finance. He does not take a degree. In the same stretch of years he serves in the United States Army, by most accounts as a court reporter taking down other men's words in shorthand, and sees no combat. Both the classroom and the stenographer's chair are rooms he passes through fast, and neither leaves a diploma or a citation behind him.
suggested_refs: City College of New York, Convent Avenue campus
sources: bob_kahn.journey.json, for the Convent Avenue coordinate

stops.name: Massachusetts, the thirty years of small ventures
stops.date_confidence: Attested in outline, undatable in detail: Wikipedia and the obituaries agree on the sequence of ventures but give no start or end dates for most of them. 1960 with defaulted month and day stands for the whole stretch from the nineteen fifties to the nineteen seventies. The coordinate is central Boston, his base through these years; individual ventures are not separately placed.
stops.campa: Through three decades he runs at business the way other men run at a wall. He makes a fortune and loses it, makes another and loses that; by his own count he is a millionaire and then not a millionaire more than once before he is fifty. Nothing in the record of these years has anything to do with casinos. What the obituaries list instead is toiletry kits sold in bulk, a windshield spray called De-Ice-It, mortgage brokering, charter tours, real estate, and trade magazines, none of them separately dated anywhere reached.
suggested_refs: De-Ice-It, the windshield product, among the ventures listed in every obituary of the early career

stops.name: The MGM Grand, Las Vegas, the first COMDEX
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Wikipedia, 'Comdex', gives the first show as 3 December 1979 with 167 exhibitors and 3,904 attendees, and the Las Vegas Review-Journal retrospective gives roughly 4,000 attendees. The coordinate is corrected here: the 1979 MGM Grand is today's Horseshoe Las Vegas at 3645 South Las Vegas Boulevard, and the dossier's 36.1094 pin fell some 350 metres south of it.
stops.campa: With four partners in the Interface Group he opens the Computer Dealers' Exposition in the ballrooms of the MGM Grand: one hundred sixty-seven exhibitors, three thousand nine hundred and four attendees, an industry that does not yet know it is one. COMDEX grows into the largest technology trade show on earth and teaches him the arithmetic everything else will be built on. The money is not in the machines on the tables. It is in owning the room the tables are standing in.
suggested_refs: The COMDEX exhibitor directories, 1979 onward
sources: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 'Adelson parlayed Comdex computer conference into integrated-resort empire'

stops.name: The Sands Hotel, the Rat Pack's house bought
stops.date_confidence: Attested year, defaulted month and day. Wikipedia, 'Sands Hotel and Casino', has MGM Grand, Inc. buying the Sands in 1988 bundled with the Desert Inn for $167 million and selling it the following year for $110 million to Las Vegas Sands. The dossier's $110 to $128 million range is not supported and the upper figure is dropped. Las Vegas Sands Corp. itself was formed 17 November 1988 with the same partners.
stops.campa: Adelson and his partners buy the Sands Hotel and Casino for one hundred ten million dollars from MGM Grand, Inc., which had taken it the year before in a bundle with the Desert Inn. The Sands is old and tired and famous: Sinatra's house, the Rat Pack's stage, a Strip landmark selling nostalgia to a city that has stopped buying it. He is fifty-five and has never run a casino in his life. The holding company formed for the purchase is called Las Vegas Sands.
suggested_refs: The Sands Hotel and Casino, opened 1952, and its Copa Room

stops.name: The Sands Expo, the convention hall behind the hotel
stops.date_confidence: Attested: Wikipedia, 'Sands Expo', gives 9 November 1990 and describes it as the only privately owned and operated convention center in the United States and the second largest in the world. The dossier's phrasing, 'largest privately owned convention facility in the United States', garbles two different superlatives and is not used.
stops.campa: On the lot behind the hotel he opens the Sands Expo and Convention Center, the only privately owned and operated convention center in the United States and the second largest in the world. Every other operator on the Strip treats conventions as filler for the weekdays when the gamblers are at work. He treats the gamblers as filler. The hall books its trade shows into the weekdays, and the hotel rooms behind it fill Monday through Thursday with people whose employers are paying.
suggested_refs: The Sands Expo and Convention Center, opened 9 November 1990
sources: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 'Adelson parlayed Comdex computer conference into integrated-resort empire'

stops.name: Las Vegas, COMDEX sold to SoftBank
stops.date_confidence: Attested month and year, defaulted day. The reported price varies across accounts between about $800 million and $862 million and Adelson's personal share is estimated rather than filed; no primary transaction document was reached in this pass. The coordinate is the Sands Expo, the Interface Group's own building, not a signing room.
stops.campa: The Interface Group partners sell COMDEX and their other exhibition properties to Masayoshi Son's SoftBank. Reported totals run from eight hundred million to eight hundred sixty-two million dollars and no filing settles which is right; Adelson's own share is put above five hundred million. He has sold the show that taught him the business. The money goes into the ground of the Strip, into a building not yet designed, on a site still occupied by a hotel with a gaming license and a Copa Room.
suggested_refs: The 1995 SoftBank acquisition of the Interface Group's trade-show business

stops.name: Piazza San Marco, the honeymoon and the idea
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction, and a correction. Wikipedia, 'Miriam Adelson', has the blind date in 1989 and the marriage in 1991, so the honeymoon falls in 1991 and the dossier's chronology lens, which put it in 1989, contradicts itself. Month and day are defaults. The claim that the Venetian was conceived in this square is corporate origin narrative with no independent witness.
stops.campa: He marries Miriam Farbstein Ochshorn, an Israeli physician he met on a blind date two years earlier, and the two go to Venice. In the piazza, according to the story the company has told ever since, they work out what it would take to put this city down in the desert: the canals, the campanile, the arcades, at a scale no European republic ever attempted. The account is corporate scripture and no witness outside the family confirms it. He comes home and starts buying drawings.
suggested_refs: The Piazza San Marco, the Doge's Palace, and the campanile, all later reproduced on the Las Vegas Strip
sources: Las Vegas Sands corporate history, sands.com/company/our-story

stops.name: The Strip, the Sands imploded
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: the hotel closed in June 1996 and was imploded on 26 November 1996. The date is convergent across the dossier chronology and the Venetian construction timeline; contemporaneous wire coverage of the implosion was not fetched directly in this pass.
stops.campa: The Sands has been closed since June. On the night after Thanksgiving the charges go off and the Rat Pack's hotel comes down into its own footprint, in front of a crowd standing along Las Vegas Boulevard. It takes about nine seconds and is filmed from six angles. The Copa Room where Sinatra sang goes with it, and so does the only part of the property anyone ever came to look at. What Adelson keeps is the name, the gaming license, the convention hall behind the site, and the dirt.
suggested_refs: Film footage of the Sands implosion, 26 November 1996

stops.name: The Venetian, ground broken on the Sands site
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'The Venetian Las Vegas', gives groundbreaking on 14 April 1997 and a cost of roughly $1.5 billion.
stops.campa: Ground is broken for the Venetian on the cleared Sands site: one and a half billion dollars, three thousand suites, a quarter mile of indoor canal. He has put the whole proceeds of COMDEX into a building he has no experience operating, and the convention space is the point while the canals are the bait. The drawings call for gondolas with gondoliers on salary, and for replicas of the Doge's Palace, the Rialto and the campanile, stacked against one another in an order Venice never had.
suggested_refs: The Venetian Resort Las Vegas, 3355 South Las Vegas Boulevard

stops.name: The Venetian sidewalk, the Culinary and the congressman
stops.date_confidence: Attested day, and a correction: Wikipedia, 'The Venetian Las Vegas', gives 1 March 1999 for the picket of more than 1,000 Culinary members. The dossier's geography lens dated it to February 1999 and contradicts its own chronology lens; the March date is used.
stops.campa: More than a thousand members of Culinary Workers Union Local 226 picket the sidewalk in front of the unfinished resort. The Culinary has organized nearly every large house on the Strip and will spend the next twenty years failing to organize this one; the sidewalk under their feet goes to court over whether it is public ground at all. Congressman John Lewis walks the line with them that day. Adelson will not meet Lewis, because the meeting on offer includes union representatives, and he does not meet with union representatives.
suggested_refs: Culinary Workers Union Local 226 institutional history of the Venetian campaign

stops.name: The Venetian, opening just after midnight
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'The Venetian Las Vegas', gives a private soft opening on the evening of 3 May 1999 and the public opening just after midnight on 4 May.
stops.campa: The Venetian opens just after midnight, following a private evening for invited guests, gondoliers singing in a chlorinated canal built on the second floor and the sky over the shopping arcade painted to hold a permanent late afternoon. The building has cost one and a half billion dollars. It works at once: conventions fill the weekdays, tourists fill the weekends, and the prototype he will carry to Macau and to Singapore is now standing on the ground where the Sands stood.
suggested_refs: The Grand Canal Shoppes and the painted sky of the Venetian arcade
sources: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 'Adelson parlayed Comdex computer conference into integrated-resort empire'

stops.name: Las Vegas, the nerves go
stops.date_confidence: Attested year across convergent obituary accounts, with no month, day, or clinical source reached; treated as attested only on the strength of that convergence, and placed first within 2001 as an ordering device rather than on evidence that it preceded the Boston decision. The coordinate is the Venetian, his workplace, because no source reached names where the diagnosis was made. Whether this illness bears any relation to the later lymphoma is not established anywhere reached.
stops.campa: He is diagnosed with peripheral neuropathy, a degeneration of the nerves that will take away his ability to stand or to walk any distance. Within a few years he crosses his own casino floors on a motorized scooter, and he gives depositions and testimony seated. He is sixty-eight, worth several billion dollars, and about to begin the largest construction program of his life on the other side of the world. The illness does not slow any of it down; it changes how he arrives. No source reached says when in the year the diagnosis came, or where, or whether it bears any relation to the lymphoma of his last years.
suggested_refs: Photographs of Adelson on the Venetian floor by scooter, from the mid-2000s onward
sources: Convergent obituary accounts, 2021, synthesized in the research dossier; no primary medical or contemporaneous source located

stops.name: Boston, the sons in Superior Court
stops.date_confidence: Attested filing date for the trial decision, and a correction the dossier got backward. CourtListener has Adelson v. Adelson, Massachusetts Superior Court, Zobel J., 13 Mass. L. Rptr. 171, filed 18 April 2001, as the only opinion carrying the phrase 'paternal kindliness'; the Massachusetts Appeals Court affirmance is the separate 2004 event at 60 Mass. App. Ct. 753. The coordinate is the Pemberton Square courthouse.
stops.campa: Two of his sons, Mitchell and Gary, sue him in Massachusetts over a family stock transaction they say defrauded them. Judge Zobel finds for the father: Adelson may have lacked paternal kindliness, the decision says, but he did not commit fraud, and the Appeals Court affirms three years later. Mitchell, who has used heroin and cocaine for years, dies in 2005. Afterward the family funds addiction treatment and spends heavily against the legalization of marijuana.
suggested_refs: Adelson v. Adelson, 13 Mass. L. Rptr. 171 (Super. Ct. 2001), and 60 Mass. App. Ct. 753 (2004)
sources: CourtListener, Adelson v. Adelson (Mass. Super. Ct., Zobel J., 18 April 2001)

stops.name: Beijing, the Vice Premier and the middleman
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The meetings with Vice Premier Qian Qichen and other officials are known chiefly through testimony in Richard Suen's Nevada litigation, summarized in the Nevada Supreme Court record; no primary filing was fetched in this pass and the year has no attested month or day. The Great Hall of the People coordinate is the dossier's reconstruction of a venue no source reached names.
stops.campa: Macau's gaming monopoly is ending and the concessions will be handed out by men in Beijing. Adelson goes to them, carried in by an intermediary named Richard Suen, and meets Vice Premier Qian Qichen among other officials. What was said in those rooms is argued over for the next twenty years in a Nevada courtroom, where Suen sues for a share of whatever the access turned out to be worth. Sands takes a Macau subconcession the following year and starts digging before anyone else does.
suggested_refs: Richard Suen v. Las Vegas Sands, Nevada Supreme Court, case 58740
sources: Nevada Supreme Court record in Suen v. Las Vegas Sands, summarized at law.justia.com (not fetched directly)

stops.name: Sands Macao, the first American house in China
stops.date_confidence: Attested day and cost: Wikipedia, 'Sands Macao', gives an opening of 18 May 2004 at a cost of $240 million, with all construction mortgage bonds paid off in May 2005. The dossier's '$240 to $265 million' range is dropped; the upper figure is unsourced. Coordinate matches the infobox within about 100 metres.
stops.campa: Sands Macao opens on the peninsula: two hundred forty million dollars of gaming floor with almost no rooms and no theme at all, the first American-operated casino in Chinese territory. The tables are full from the opening day. He has found a market where nobody needs to be persuaded to sit down and play, and where the players do not want a show. The house earns back its construction cost within about a year, and every mortgage bond issued to build it is retired in May 2005.

stops.name: The New York Stock Exchange, six point eight percent sold
stops.date_confidence: Attested month and year, defaulted day. Wikipedia, 'Las Vegas Sands', gives the December 2004 New York Stock Exchange listing at $29 a share with 6.8 percent of the company offered; the dossier's '6.8 to 12 percent' range is dropped. The Forbes net-worth figure for 2007 was not re-fetched from the Forbes archive in this pass.
stops.campa: Las Vegas Sands goes public on the New York Stock Exchange at twenty-nine dollars a share under the ticker LVS, with six point eight percent of the company offered and everything else held by Adelson and his partners. The stock rises on the first day and keeps rising. Because he sold so little of it, the fortune the market prints is almost entirely the Macau earnings capitalized forward. Three years later Forbes puts him third in America at about twenty-six and a half billion dollars.

stops.name: Marina Bay, the bid submitted alone
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'Marina Bay Sands', gives 27 May 2006 as the date Las Vegas Sands was declared winner of the Marina Bay integrated resort bid, submitted without the local partner that had withdrawn.
stops.campa: Singapore, having decided to permit casinos for the first time, opens bidding for an integrated resort on reclaimed land at Marina Bay. Adelson's local partner withdraws before submission and he files alone. The government declares Las Vegas Sands the winner. What he has promised them is not a casino but a national landmark with a casino inside it: three towers by Moshe Safdie carrying a ship-shaped garden across their roofs, a museum shaped like an open hand, and a convention hall underneath the whole thing.

stops.name: The Cotai Strip, the Venetian built twice
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'The Venetian Macao', gives 28 August 2007. The $2.4 billion cost is carried by the dossier chronology and does not appear in the Wikipedia article; it was not verified in this pass. Coordinate corrected to the infobox value, 22 degrees 8 minutes 55 seconds north by 113 degrees 33 minutes 38 seconds east; the dossier's pin was about 420 metres off.
stops.campa: On reclaimed land between Coloane and Taipa, ground he has promoted and trademarked as the Cotai Strip, the Venetian Macao opens: the Doge's Palace again, the canals again, three thousand suites, a gaming floor larger than any other on earth. The Las Vegas building has become a prototype, and the copy is bigger than the original, standing on land that did not exist a decade ago. The cost is reported at two point four billion dollars, a figure no filing reached confirms. He is seventy-four, and the convention halls underneath are the part he talks about.

stops.name: Yad Vashem, the twenty-five million
stops.date_confidence: Attested day by the institution's own press release of 26 October 2006, which returned 403 on fetch and was not read directly; the gift is corroborated by JTA, 'For Sheldon Adelson, political and Jewish giving are all of a piece' (fetched). The coordinate is Yad Vashem on the Mount Herzl ridge.
stops.campa: Sheldon and Miriam Adelson pledge twenty-five million dollars to Yad Vashem, on the ridge of Mount Herzl, where the state keeps its record of the murdered. It is the first of the very large Israeli gifts and it sets the pattern for the rest: Birthright flights, the Friends of the Israel Defense Forces, a medical research foundation, a school in Herzliya that carries his name. He gives as an American donor, and he gives to the institutions that hold the national account of what was done to the Jews of Europe.

stops.name: Tel Aviv, Israel Hayom given away free
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'Israel Hayom', gives the launch as 30 July 2007, at least $50 million of Adelson's money at the start and roughly $190 million in accumulated losses between 2007 and 2014. Coordinate corrected to the offices Wikipedia names, 2 Ha-Shlosha Street; the dossier's pin sat about 2.3 kilometres away in the city centre.
stops.campa: He launches Israel Hayom, a national daily handed out free on the streets of every Israeli city and printed at a loss he covers himself: fifty million dollars to start it and something near one hundred ninety million in accumulated losses across its first seven years. Paid competitors cannot compete with a price of nothing. Within a few years it is the most read paper in the country, and its line on benjamin_netanyahu is so unwavering that Israelis call it the Bibiton, the Bibi paper.

stops.name: Las Vegas, the year the company nearly goes
stops.date_confidence: Attested month and year for the covenant warning, defaulted day; the debt figure, the share price collapse, and the family's roughly $1 billion capital injection come from contemporaneous financial reporting synthesized in the dossier and were not re-fetched from a primary filing in this pass. The quote is verbatim from a Wall Street Journal blog post of 22 November 2010, two years after the events described here.
stops.campa: Las Vegas Sands carries roughly eight point eight billion dollars of long-term debt into the autumn, warns its investors in November that it may breach its covenants, and states plainly that bankruptcy is possible. The stock, above one hundred forty dollars the year before, goes under two. The Palazzo has opened next door to the Venetian in these same months, into a market that has stopped arriving. The family puts about a billion dollars of its own money back into the company to hold it upright.
stops.quote: So I lost $25 billion. I started out with zero ...[there is] no such thing as fear, not to an entrepreneur. Concern, yes. Fear, no.

stops.name: Marina Bay Sands, the towers opened in phases
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: Wikipedia, 'Marina Bay Sands', gives a phased opening from 27 April 2010 and a cost escalating from an initial S$3.85 billion commitment toward roughly S$8 billion, about US$6.88 billion, through the financial crisis.
stops.campa: Marina Bay Sands opens in phases, the casino floor first, its cost having climbed from a promised three point eight five billion Singapore dollars toward eight billion while the crisis ran through the construction. He did not stop building when the money stopped, and the property earns at a rate that repays the whole gamble. Safdie's three towers carry a garden across their roofs, and the whole thing stands on ground Singapore reclaimed from the sea.

stops.name: Macau, the chief executive dismissed
stops.date_confidence: Attested month and year, defaulted day: Wikipedia, 'Las Vegas Sands', places the dismissal of Steven C. Jacobs in July 2010 and his Nevada suit in October. The coordinate is Sands Macao, the operating base of the subsidiary he ran; no source reached names where the dismissal took place.
stops.campa: Sands dismisses Steven Jacobs, president and chief executive of its Macau subsidiary. Jacobs sues in Nevada that October, saying he was fired for refusing instructions: that he was told to run secret surveillance on Macau officials and to keep on a lawyer who was also a Macau legislator, Leonel Alves. The suit will run six years and put Adelson in a Las Vegas witness box. Along the way the internal correspondence of Sands China enters the public record of two jurisdictions.

stops.name: Israel, the Birthright group and the invented people

stops.campa: Speaking to a group of young American Jews brought to Israel on flights his money pays for, Adelson tells them what he thinks of the people on the other side of the line, borrowing the formula from a presidential candidate he is at that moment keeping in the race. He is the largest private donor to Birthright, whose trip is sold to its participants as a free holiday, and what they hear on it is whatever the donor decides to come and say. Nothing reached names the room he said it in. Revital Blumenfeld has the remark in Haaretz inside a fortnight, and it travels from there.
stops.quote: read the history of those who call themselves Palestinians, and you will hear why Gingrich said recently that the Palestinians are an invented people.

stops.name: The Venetian, six minutes on a congressman
stops.date_confidence: Attested month and year from JTA's reporting on TribeFest, defaulted day. The $93.3 million super PAC total for the 2012 cycle is the figure carried in the dossier from contemporaneous campaign-finance reporting and was not re-fetched from a Federal Election Commission record in this pass.
stops.campa: TribeFest convenes in his own Venetian, and the surrogates of both parties argue in front of a Jewish audience about which one Israel should prefer. Adelson takes the floor and spends six minutes working over a Democratic congressman, a luxury an organizer afterward says no one else in the room would have been granted. Candidates now fly to Las Vegas to audition in front of him. He has given ninety-three point three million dollars to super PACs this cycle, much of it to keep Newt Gingrich's candidacy breathing past the point where it should have stopped.

stops.name: Alcorcon, the Madrid casino that is not built
stops.date_confidence: Attested year only, month and day defaulted per convention; the abandonment was announced late in 2013 but no source fetched in this pass gives the day, and the Spanish and international business reporting behind the account was not fetched directly. stops.name: Yeshiva University, the weapon in the desert
stops.date_confidence: Attested day: the panel is dated 22 October 2013, with the remarks reported by the Times of Israel on 24 October and by the Jewish Press the same week. The Jewish Press original returned 404 on fetch; the quote was read verbatim in Wikipedia's cited wikitext. The Times of Israel report gives a slightly different transcription, 'cellphone' for 'cell phone', which is left unresolved here.
stops.campa: At a Yeshiva University panel on Iran, asked what the United States should do, he proposes a demonstration. Detonate an American warhead in an empty stretch of Iranian desert, he says, kill nothing but scorpions, and then telephone Tehran. He is eighty years old and the largest donor in the Republican Party, and the room he is saying this in is a university hall in upper Manhattan. His spokesman later calls the remarks hyperbole. Two papers report the sentence and neither transcribes it quite the way the other does.
stops.quote: You pick up your cell phone and you call somewhere in Nebraska and you say 'OK, let it go' and so there's an atomic weapon goes over, ballistic missiles in the middle of the desert that doesn't hurt a soul, maybe a couple of rattlesnakes and scorpions or whatever.
